last.verdict: EVgo cut its 2026 outlook again, but a $2.00-a-share buyout bid from controlling owner LS Power now matters more than the results.

takeaways.label: Buyout bid
takeaways.text: LS Power, which holds about 56% of the voting power, offered $2.00 a share in cash on Nov. 2. It is non-binding, and a special committee is reviewing it.

takeaways.label: Second guidance cut
takeaways.text: 2026 revenue outlook fell to $375-400M from $400-430M, and the adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $15-30M from $5-25M. Stalls added are guided to 1,075-1,275.

takeaways.label: Core growing, total flat
takeaways.text: Charging revenue rose 29% to $72M, but total revenue slipped 1% to $91.4M as revenue from building chargers for partners (eXtend) fell 49%. Per-stall daily throughput dipped to 283 kWh from 295.

takeaways.label: Losses and cash drain
takeaways.text: Net loss grew to $49.2M from $28.4M, with admin costs up 39%. Cash fell to $99M from $151M over nine months while debt rose to about $317M from $207M.

history.verdict: Investors sold EVgo after the company cut its full-year outlook and cash burn rose.

reasons.label: Lower 2026 outlook
reasons.text: Revenue guidance cut to $400-430M from $410-470M; below analysts' roughly $433M.

reasons.label: Bigger expected losses
reasons.text: Full-year adjusted EBITDA now a $5-25M loss, versus a range reaching up to +$20M before.

reasons.label: Cash and slower ramp
reasons.text: Operating cash burn widened and new stalls ramped slower than hoped, despite Tesla deal.
